To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
fucosylated type I TGF-βR enhances TGF-β signalling, leading to induction of EMT in CRC cells.
fucosylated type I TGF-βR is essential for TGF-β-induced EMT in CRC cells.
fucosylated type I TGF-βR is a key mediator of TGF-ß-induced epithelial–meschymal transition in CRC cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of FucT3/6 in TGF-β-induced EMT and the migration of CRC cells.
the molecular mechanism of fucosylated sialyl Lewis antigen in cancer progression.
the identification of a novel mechanism of fucosylation in CRC metastasis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FUT3/ FUT6 is a novel target in CRC and could be used for the development of new therapeutics for the disease.
FUT3/ 6 plays a critical role in cancer cell migration and adhesion to endothelium by upregulation and fucosylation, respectively, of sialyl lewis antigens, and by enhancing EMT in CRC cells.
the fucosylated sialyl Lewis antigen is a key molecule that regulates cancer cell adhesion and migration by two independent pathways.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
FUT3 and/or FUT6 expression is a potential therapeutic target for the treatment of CRC.
FUT3/ FUT6-mediated fucosylation plays a crucial role in the metastasis of CRC through TGF- β-mediated EMT.
the inhibition of FUT3 or FUT6 by siRNAs suppresses the fucosylated type I TGF-β1 receptor, which leads to inhibition of TGF-1-induced EMT in CRC cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fucosylated form of TβR1 is a novel regulator of TGF-ß-mediated EMT and metastasis.
the expression of FUT3, FUT6 and fucosylated sialyl Lewis antigen is a marker of tumour progression and metastasis.
the inhibition of fucosylated receptors by FUT3/ 6 siRNAs can be a novel therapeutic target for the treatment of CRC.
